title: Strategic Account Quarterly playbook & meeting kit
summary: A lightweight, facilitator-friendly QBR kit for Strategic / Enterprise accounts. Purpose: align on realized value, knock down open blockers, and co-create next-quarter priorities with explicit renewal and expansion signals. Designed for a 60-90 minute working session with an executive sponsor and functional leads. Not prescriptive cadence; meant to be adaptable by account maturity (early adoption vs. expansion vs. pre-renewal).
agenda_items: 0-5m: Welcome + goals (host intro, set outcomes & timebox; confirm attendees and roles)
5-15m: Customer context & wins (customer shares top outcomes since last QBR; CSM summarizes major milestones)
15-30m: Usage & outcomes dashboard (walk through key metrics: latency/cost per token improvements, feature adoption, error rates; call out anomalies)
30-45m: Support & reliability review (incident recap, MTTR trends, ongoing SRE/engineering workstreams)
45-60m: Roadmap alignment & co-innovation opportunities (product team presents 2–3 roadmap items and ask for priorities)
60-75m: Commercial check-in (contract timeline, renewal signals, pricing levers, expansion ideas)
75-85m: Risk triage & mitigation (explicit decisions, owners, decision deadlines)
85-90m: Recap & next steps (confirm actions, owners, dates; schedule follow-up)
facilitation_script: Opening (host): Thank you all for joining. Our goal for the next 60–90 minutes is to ensure you feel measurable progress toward the outcomes we committed to, identify any gaps blocking adoption/expansion, and leave with 3 concrete actions and owners. Any additions to the goals?
Transition to wins: Avery -> Jordan: Jordan, can you kick us off with the top customer wins you've seen since our last check-in? Keep to 3 items and the impact (quantified if possible).

Metrics walkthrough prompt: 'We’ll run through the success metrics snapshot next. For each metric I’ll state current value, trend, and what a 1–2x improvement would unlock for your team. If anything looks surprising, call it out and we’ll pause.'

Incident recap prompt: 'SRE/Support will summarize incidents and mitigations. For each incident, we want root cause, user impact, mitigation applied, and what permanence (release/rollout/monitoring) is planned.'
Roadmap alignment prompt: 'Product has 3 candidate priorities that align with your asks. We’ll present them briefly, then ask you to rank 1–2 that deliver the most customer value this year.'

Commercial/renewal prompt: 'We’ll review the renewal window, current ARR footprint, and any expansion opportunities. We’re not having a pricing negotiation today, just aligning on timing and priorities that will influence terms.'

Risk triage facilitation: 'For any red/yellow signals, I’ll ask the owning stakeholder to propose a 30/60/90-day mitigation plan with concrete owner, deliverable, and a decision date. We’ll capture that as an action in the last 5 minutes.'
Closing: 'Quick read-back of actions: who, what, when. I will send a follow-up note with decisions and calendar invites for any deep-dive follow-ups. Thanks everyone.'
meeting_prep_checklist: Send pre-read 5 business days prior: one-page metrics snapshot, top-3 wins, top-3 blockers, and current contract summary
Collect and attach a graph pack: weekly active integrations, inference P95 latency, average tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, error volume (last 90 days)
Request customer to prepare a 2-slide 'outcomes achieved' doc if they want to present customer perspective
Invite list: exec sponsor, technical lead, procurement/finance (if renewal within 90 days), CSM, AE, Solutions Eng, Product PM (optional)
Confirm meeting owner/facilitator and scribe — ensure scribe has doc template and can capture action items live
Validate access: share dashboards and logs links ahead, ensure attendees have permissions to view private sheets/dashboards
Run tech check 15 minutes before (video, screen share, presenter order); prepare breakout link if necessary
Pre-run risk scoring: CSM to fill preliminary risk signal checklist and suggested mitigation prior to meeting
renewal_tracker_template: columns: Account | Renewal date | Contract term | ARR / ACV | Current TCV | Renewal owner | Risk score (1-5) | Primary risk drivers | Action required | Next checkpoint date
example-row: AcmeCorp | 2026-06-30 | 12m | $350,000 | $350k | Marco Alvarez | 3 | Usage plateau, open P1 bug, procurement timeline | Exec alignment, feature delivery comms | 2026-05-01
success_metrics_snapshot: Adoption: active integrations (DAU/MAU style for inference endpoints) — include 90d trend
Reliability: P95 latency, error rate (5xx + client errors), incident count & MTTR
Cost & efficiency: average cost per 1k tokens, trend vs baseline after quantization/batching changes
Business outcomes: feature-led KPIs the customer cares about (e.g., search relevance improvement, time-to-completion, conversion impact)
Qualitative: NPS / customer sentiment notes from support and AE conversations (last 90d)
risk_signals: Usage flat or declining for 2+ quarters despite new initiatives
Major unresolved P1/P0 older than SLA for >30 days
Procurement or legal delays >60 days from expected renewal trigger
Significant negative spike in latency or error rate after a release
Multiple internal stakeholders disengaged / exec sponsor changed and not yet onboarded
follow_up_templates: Post-QBR summary email: Hi {{Sponsor}}, thanks for the time today. Attached are meeting notes, agreed actions, owners and due dates. Highlights: 1) Exec alignment on priority X; 2) Support committed to fix Y by DATE; 3) Next checkpoint scheduled for DATE. Action owner list attached. - Avery

Action reminder (7 days before checkpoint): Hi {{Owner}}, quick reminder about the action '{{Action}}' due {{DueDate}}. Please update the shared doc with progress and blockers. Happy to pair if you need help. - CSM
Renewal nudges (90/60/30 days): Template with attachable 'value map' and usage highlights; include ask for procurement timeline and decision owner
notes_for_CSM: Practical tips: 1) Quantify value wherever possible (e.g., tokens saved, latency improvements tied to conversion), 2) Use risk scoring to drive a single-threaded owner for mitigation, 3) Avoid pricing negotiation in QBR unless commercial stakeholders are present and prepared, 4) Capture 'showstoppers' as binary decisions with decision dates, 5) Follow-up with tailored one-pagers for execs (2 slides) and technical teams (detailed runbook)
operational_handoff: After the QBR, CSM to update renewal tracker row, create Jira epic for any engineering deliverable, and assign a 30/60/90 day success plan in the customer's workspace
preferred_meeting_length: 60-90 minutes depending on complexity and near-term renewal timeline
notes: This is a working draft. Use as a scaffold and customize language to the account. Capture version and date when saving a copy for a customer record.
